answerCheck.reason: Linear combinations of coplanar vectors remain in their common plane and cannot span all of three-dimensional space.
Subtracting two representations would give a zero linear combination of basis vectors. Their linear independence forces all corresponding coefficients to be equal.

routes.label: Use uniqueness for a fixed basis

answerCheck.reason: Three-dimensional space has dimension 3, so a basis consists of three noncoplanar vectors.

answerCheck.derivedAnswer: A (All three corresponding components must be equal)
answerCheck.reason: If two equal vectors had different corresponding coordinates, they would have two different representations in the same basis, contradicting uniqueness.
